His mathematical techniques, which he systematically used and accepted as solutions and coefficients, were later adopted by Fibonacci, thus playing a crucial role in introducing algebra to Europe.

Shujāʿ ibn Aslam's contributions to mathematics were groundbreaking, and his work had a profound impact on the development of mathematics in the Middle Ages. His work on algebra, in particular, helped to establish the field as a major area of study, paving the way for future mathematicians to build upon his discoveries.

As a key figure in the transmission of knowledge from the Middle East to Europe, Shujāʿ ibn Aslam's work had far-reaching consequences, influencing the development of mathematics and science in the Western world. His legacy continues to be felt today, with his contributions to algebra remaining an essential part of the history of mathematics.

The impact of Shujāʿ ibn Aslam's work can be seen in the many mathematicians who followed in his footsteps, including Fibonacci, who was heavily influenced by his work. The adoption of algebra in Europe during the Middle Ages was a direct result of Shujāʿ ibn Aslam's contributions, and his work continues to be studied and admired by mathematicians around the world.
